title: GTA 6 Sales: $3.79 Billion on Day One, What Take-Two Reported
desc: Take-Two says GTA 6 hit $3.79 billion in day one retail sales and 32.5 million units sold before launch. How that compares to GTA 5 and what Take-Two keeps.
keywords: gta 6 sales, how much has gta 6 made, gta 6 day one sales, gta 6 $3.79 billion, gta 6 units sold, gta 6 vs gta 5 sales, take-two gta 6 revenue, who owns gta 6, gta 6 net bookings
question: How much has GTA 6 made so far, according to Take-Two?
cta: Planning a product launch with pre-orders and alerts?
body:
Short answer. Take-Two Interactive says Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) reached $3.79 billion in day one retail sales, based on its own worldwide estimates through the end of November 19, 2026, the launch day. It also says the game sold 32.5 million units before release. Take-Two calls it the biggest entertainment launch in history across any medium.

On November 23, 2026 we read Take-Two's own press releases and its latest quarterly results, plus its 2013 filing on Grand Theft Auto V. Every company figure below links to its source. We do not give stock advice; this guide reports what the company said and explains what the numbers mean.

What Take-Two reported after launch

In a release dated November 20, 2026, Take-Two and Rockstar Games announced that GTA 6 "day one retail sales" reached $3.79 billion. A footnote says the figure is "based on company estimates through end of day November 19th worldwide". Take-Two describes it as day one retail sales based on its own estimates. It is not an audited revenue number.

The same release says GTA 6 sold 32.5 million units before release, which Take-Two calls a record across all platforms, and it cites a score of 99 on Metacritic. Sam Houser, President and Founder of Rockstar Games, said in the release that the studio enters "a new chapter" with the game.

GTA 6 went on sale on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, through the PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, Rockstar Games Store and retailers. The launch announcement lists only PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S; no PC version has been announced in these releases.

How it compares to GTA 5's first day

The closest yardstick is Rockstar's own last launch. On September 18, 2013, Take-Two told investors in an SEC filing that Grand Theft Auto V had first day sell-through of more than $800 million worldwide, excluding its later launch in Japan and Brazil. GTA 5 came out on September 17, 2013, on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, and more than 8,300 stores in North America opened at midnight for it.

Put side by side, $3.79 billion is roughly 4.7 times $800 million, and because GTA 5's figure was "more than" $800 million, 4.7 times is an upper bound. Treat that as a rough guide only: both figures are company estimates, they are in dollars of different years (not adjusted for inflation), and the 2013 number left out two countries.

LaunchGTA 5GTA 6
Launch dateSeptember 17, 2013November 19, 2026
First day sales (company estimate)More than $800 million$3.79 billion
Scope of the estimateWorldwide, excluding Japan and BrazilWorldwide, through end of day November 19
Platforms at launchPlayStation 3, Xbox 360PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S
Units sold before launchNot given in the release32.5 million

For context on the long tail, Take-Two's November 20, 2026 release says GTA 5 has sold in nearly 235 million units (sell-in is Take-Two's term for copies shipped to stores plus digital sales), and its June 2026 pre-order release put the whole Grand Theft Auto series at over 470 million units sold in.

You may also have seen a lower figure. Sensor Tower, an outside tracker, estimated about $1.84 billion in sales and roughly 19 million copies by release day, as FOX 5 DC reported on November 19, 2026. That was a third party estimate made before the end of launch day. Take-Two's $3.79 billion is the company's own worldwide estimate through the end of November 19, so the two numbers do not measure the same thing.

Retail sales are not what Take-Two keeps

This is the part most headlines skip. The $3.79 billion is a retail sales figure, Take-Two's estimate of sales at stores and storefronts. Take-Two's own results use a different measure called Net Bookings, which its second quarter release defines as "the net amount of products and services sold digitally or sold-in physically during the period".

The gap matters because sales through third party stores and console storefronts are typically subject to platform or retailer margins, while sales on the Rockstar Games Store are not. Take-Two has not published how much of the $3.79 billion it will book, so any split you see elsewhere is an estimate, not a company number.

That is also why the $3.79 billion cannot be compared directly with Take-Two's full year outlook. On November 9, 2026, ten days before launch, Take-Two reiterated that it expects Net Bookings of $8.0 to $8.2 billion for its fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, and gave an outlook of $3.35 to $3.5 billion in Net Bookings for the three months ending December 31, 2026. Those ranges cover all of the company's games, including NBA 2K and its mobile titles, and they were set before the launch figure was known. Our earlier guide on how much money GTA 6 will make walks through that outlook in more detail.

Where the money comes from: price and editions

According to the pre-order release of June 24, 2026, GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the standard game and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition, which adds vehicles, weapons, clothing and other items. Pre-orders opened at midnight local time on June 25, 2026, and digital pre-order buyers could start pre-loading on November 12, 2026.

Even the boxed copy points to digital. The same release says the physical version contains a download code inside the box, shipped from November 12 so players could pre-load. That fits Take-Two's wider business: in the quarter to September 30, 2026, $1,562.9 million of its $1,601.3 million in Net Bookings came from digital online sales, about 97.6 percent, according to its second quarter results.

What Take-Two has not said yet

As of November 23, 2026, the company has not published:

  • how many copies sold on launch day itself (only the 32.5 million sold before release);
  • a split by PlayStation and Xbox, or by country;
  • how much of the $3.79 billion becomes Take-Two revenue or Net Bookings;
  • any updated outlook for the fiscal year after launch.

The next scheduled place for those answers is Take-Two's third quarter results for the period ending December 31, 2026. Until then, treat any "total so far" number that is not on Take-Two's press release page as an outside estimate, and check who made it and when.

What other businesses can learn from the launch

Searches show people care about the business side: in Google Trends for the United States over the past 7 days, read on November 23, 2026, queries such as "how much has gta 6 made so far", "who owns gta6" and "is rockstar a publicly traded company" were all marked Breakout in the related queries for "take-two". Three lessons hold up without any guesswork:

  • Sell before you ship. 32.5 million units were sold before release, so demand was proven long before November 19, 2026.
  • Make the day one number easy to repeat. One clear figure, released the day after launch with a footnote saying exactly what it measures, became the headline everywhere.
  • Own the digital path. With a download code even inside the box and pre-loading a week early, launch day depended on download stores and servers more than on shelves.

Smaller brands can copy the first and third of these. A waitlist or pre-order page, plus automated emails and stock alerts when the product goes live, is the same idea at a smaller scale. If you run an online store, our AI automation for e-commerce team builds pre-order flows, launch-day alerts and order follow-ups like these.

Facts in this guide were read on November 23, 2026 on the pages linked above. Rockstar Games is a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., which trades on Nasdaq as TTWO. This guide is not investment advice.
faqs: How much money has GTA 6 made so far?

Take-Two says GTA 6 reached $3.79 billion in day one retail sales, based on company estimates through the end of November 19, 2026 worldwide. As of November 23, 2026 it had not published a newer total.
How many copies of GTA 6 have been sold?
Take-Two says GTA 6 sold 32.5 million units before release, a record across all platforms. It has not given a launch day or total unit figure yet.

Yes, by Take-Two's own figures. GTA 5 had first day sell-through of more than $800 million in 2013, excluding Japan and Brazil. GTA 6 reached $3.79 billion on day one, roughly 4.7 times as much in nominal dollars (an upper bound, since GTA 5's figure was more than $800 million).

No. It is Take-Two's estimate of day one retail sales. Sales through console storefronts and retailers are typically subject to their margins, and Take-Two reports its own results as Net Bookings. It has not said how much of the $3.79 billion it will book.
GTA 6 is made by Rockstar Games, a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. Take-Two is a public company listed on Nasdaq under the symbol TTWO.
Take-Two lists GTA 6 at $79.99 for the standard game and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
